name: Phone Call
description: Lets this agent place a real phone call for you — it dials out from the Kade-AI phone line, talks, and saves a transcript in Calls & Conversations. Calls are capped and recorded, and each one costs a little real money on the phone bill. It can't receive calls, only place them. Try: "call my pharmacy and ask if my refill is ready."

name: Push Notification
description: Lets this agent ping your phone's lock screen — reminders, check-ins, and "your long task is done" notes. It has built-in manners: quiet hours at night, cooldowns, and daily caps it cannot break. It can't text other people, only notify YOUR phone. Try: "remind me at 4 to take the bread out."

name: Agent Calls
description: Lets this agent actually CALL you — at the time you set, your phone rings with a real ringtone you pick, and answering drops you straight into a live voice call where it already knows why it called. Wake-up calls, spoken reminders, scheduled catch-ups. Quiet hours and daily caps are built in, and ringing through quiet hours only happens if you say so. Try: "call me tomorrow at 8 about my meds."

name: Diary Memory Search
description: Lets this character search your private dated diary — the long-term archive of day-to-day life it quietly keeps beside its memory cards. Ask things like "what was I up to last week?" or "have I mentioned that show before?" and it looks up the real entries instead of guessing. Each character can only see its own diary plus shared notes.

name: The World
description: Lets this character walk you through the persistent city beyond the Threshold Gate — a shared text world where your actions are real and remembered. Move, look, pick things up, talk to whoever's in the room; speak naturally or use classic commands. The world keeps its own chronicle.

name: Voice Memo Transcriber
description: Turns an uploaded voice memo or audio recording into clean, formatted text. Attach the audio to the chat, then ask the agent to transcribe or summarize it. Free to use. There's also a standalone page at /transcribe.

name: Fal Studio (Video + Design)
description: Makes short AI video clips and polished design images (posters, cards, logos — the kind where the text comes out spelled right). Each video costs real money (roughly 50 cents to a dollar per short clip), design images a few cents. It can't edit videos you upload. Try: "make a 5-second video of a corgi surfing."

name: Calculator
description: Does exact math — arithmetic, percentages, conversions — so numbers are computed, not guessed. It can't graph or solve word problems by itself; it just crunches what the agent feeds it. Try: "what's 15% of 1,240?"

name: Flux
description: Draws brand-new pictures from a description, using the site's shared image credits. It can't edit or look at photos you upload — it only creates new ones. Try: "paint me a cozy cabin in the Ozarks at sunset."

authConfig.label: Your Flux API Key
authConfig.description: Provide your Flux API key from your user profile.

name: Weather
description: Looks up real, current weather and forecasts for any city — free and instant. It can't do past weather history. Try: "what's the weather in Springfield this weekend?"

name: Location
description: Real location awareness from your own device, only while "Share my location" is on in Settings: where am I, what's around me, and spoken walking directions. Free map data (OpenStreetMap). Try: "what's around me?"

name: Media Ears & Eyes
description: Send a YouTube link or an audio/video file and the character actually takes it in — then describes what happens on screen and how the music is built: instruments, arrangement, vocals, section by section. Try: "describe this video" with a link.

name: Song Lyrics
description: Looks up song lyrics by artist and title from open lyric services (LRCLIB) — built for the job, so lyric-site bot walls can't block it. Free. Try: "pull up the lyrics to Gethsemane by Sleep Token."

name: Site Help
description: Looks up Kade-AI's own help pages so the character can explain how a feature on this site works, what it costs, what changed recently, or what to do when something breaks — from the real current page, not a guess. Free and instant. Try: "how do I turn on voice?"

name: Wikipedia
description: Looks things up on Wikipedia — people, places, history, science — so answers come from the encyclopedia instead of memory. Free. It only knows what Wikipedia knows. Try: "who was Bass Reeves?"

name: Jokes
description: Pulls fresh jokes from a live joke database — clean by default, uncensored only for adult personas. Try: "tell me a dad joke."

name: News briefing
description: Reads real, current headlines from free news feeds — national, world, Springfield/Ozarks local, tech, entertainment, music, sports. It gets headlines and summaries, not full articles. Try: "what's happening in the news this morning?"

name: Deep research
description: Real background research: many searches, many sources read and cross-checked, then a clear spoken report with numbered citations. Takes a few minutes and taps your phone when it's ready. Try: "really dig into which hearing aid brands are worth it."

name: Drive my PC
description: The platform's hands on Kade's own computer, through her screen reader — read the screen, talk in her ear, press keys, run whole errands with permission gates. Owner-only: this tool answers to Kade's own account and refuses everyone else, so adding it to another agent just gets polite no's.

name: Living memory
description: The project's living knowledge shelf, read from the memory repo. Kade's own seat reads the whole project memory; every other turn reads only the published family help docs — the seat decides, not the conversation.

name: Errands
description: Send your character off to run a real errand in the background — look things up, cross-check them, keep a step-by-step record — then come back with the answer AND how it knows. Kade's own seat only. Try: "run me an errand: find the cheapest chest freezer in Springfield."

name: Kade Council
description: Pitch an idea to Kade's five-seat AI advisory council — Aria, Prism, Sentinel, Vault, Pilgrim — and hear one composed, plain-spoken verdict with disagreements kept visible. Advisors never deciders. Kade's own seat only. Try: "pitch the council: what if rooms had themed evenings?"

name: Read a webpage
description: You share a link, it reads the page and returns just the article text — no ads, menus, or clutter. Great for having a webpage read aloud. It can't log into sites or fill out forms, and some paywalled pages won't open. Try: "read me this article" with a link pasted in.

name: Adventure save files
description: Gives story games a save file — so a text adventure or RPG can save, load, and pick up where you left off days later, even in a new conversation. Only useful for games. Try: "continue my dungeon adventure from last time."

name: Game Parlor
description: The Game Parlor: 19 voice-friendly games with a real referee keeping score — Blackjack, Uno, War, Go Fish, Farkle, Battleship, trivia, and more. The server tracks cards and dice, so the agent can't cheat or lose count. Try: "deal me some blackjack."

name: Send Feedback
description: Sends a bug report, feature idea, or general feedback straight to Kade, the person who runs this site. Free and instant. Try: "tell Kade the voice cut out during my call."

name: Family Messages
description: Takes a message for another person on this site — it's held and delivered next time they open a chat. It can't reach people outside Kade-AI (no texts or emails). Try: "tell Skylee I said happy birthday."

name: Code Runner
description: Runs a small computer program (Python, Bash, or Node) in a safe sandbox and reports what it prints — handy for exact calculations, date math, or quick data crunching. It can't reach the internet or your files. Try: "figure out how many days until Christmas."

name: Make a File
description: Makes a real spreadsheet, CSV or document you can open and keep, and saves it to your My Creations — with a spoken description of what's inside, because a file you can't see is only useful if somebody tells you what's in it. Try: "make me a spreadsheet of this month's bills."
